title: How to Clean Between the Glass on Your Oven Door
hook: Greasy streaks and dark spots trapped between the panes of your oven door can't be reached with a cloth. It's one of the most annoying cleaning problems in any kitchen. But with the right steps, you can get inside the door safely and make the glass crystal clear again. Take it slowly and it's very manageable. We also cover what to do if the door will not come apart.
intro: Most oven doors are made of two or three layers of glass, and splashes of grease get in through small vents at the top. To clean them, you need to remove the door, and take the glass apart. That sounds scary, but on most ovens it takes about thirty minutes, and requires only a screwdriver. A word of caution before we start. Door designs vary, so look at your manual or the maker's website for the exact method for your model. If your door is sealed and has no screws, don't force it, and talk to the manufacturer.
youNeedNarration: Here's what you need. A screwdriver, usually a Phillips head. Warm water and a little dish soap. Two or three microfiber cloths, and a large towel or blanket to protect the door and the table. Cotton gloves, if you have them. And your oven manual, or a photo of the door instructions from the manufacturer's website. A phone for taking photos is useful too.
heroImagePrompt: A spotless stainless steel oven with a crystal clear glass door in a modern kitchen, soft daylight, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Switch off and cool the oven
steps.narration: Step one. Turn the oven off and let it cool completely, for at least an hour. If you can, unplug it, or switch off the power at the circuit breaker, and turn off the gas if you have a gas oven. Read the part of your manual that explains how to remove the door. Take photos of the door and hinges before you touch anything, so you remember how everything fits. This is a job to do calmly and with good light. Also, remove any racks, so the oven is easier to reach. Let the lights cool, too.
steps.imagePrompt: An open oven door in a tidy kitchen with the oven empty and cool, soft window light, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Remove the oven door
steps.narration: Step two. Open the door fully, and look for the hinge locks, small metal clips or levers on each hinge. Flip them to the locked position, as shown in your manual. Then close the door gently until it stops at about fifteen degrees, grip both sides, and lift it up and out towards you. The door is heavier than it looks, so ask someone to help if needed. Lay it flat on a towel on a table or the floor, with the handle facing you. If you can't find the locks, search the oven's model number online. A short video of your exact model can help.
steps.mistake: Lifting the door without locking the hinges
steps.imagePrompt: Two hands lifting a heavy oven door away from its hinges in a kitchen, towel on the table nearby, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Open the top of the door
steps.narration: Step three. Look at the top edge of the door, where there is usually a metal trim with two or three screws, or clips on the sides. Remove the screws, and set them aside in a cup, so they do not roll away. Lift off the trim carefully. You will then see the inner glass panes, which slide out or lift out, held by small clips or rubber spacers. Keep track of the order of every part, taking a photo as you go. Tip the door gently to see if the trim moves. Keep the door flat, so the glass doesn't slide out suddenly.
steps.tip: Use a cup for the screws
steps.mistake: Forcing a clip that has not released
steps.imagePrompt: A screwdriver removing screws from the top trim of an oven door lying on a towel, close-up, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Slide out the glass panes
steps.narration: Step four. Carefully slide out the middle pane or panes, handling them by the edges, with both hands. Wear gloves, as glass edges can be sharp. Lay each pane on a clean towel, in order, and remember which side faced which way. Some panes have a coating on one side, so note the orientation. If anything feels stuck, stop and check your manual. Never force glass. If a pane is cracked, don't reuse it. Place a soft cloth between the panes while they're stacked, if you must set them down together, so they don't scratch each other.
steps.mistake: Gripping glass by the face with wet hands
steps.imagePrompt: Gloved hands carefully sliding a glass pane out of an oven door, towel on the table, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Wash the glass
steps.narration: Step five. Wash each pane in warm water with a little dish soap, using a soft sponge or a microfiber cloth. Burnt-on spots can be soaked with a paste of baking soda and water for fifteen minutes, then gently wiped. Never use steel wool, scouring powders or razor blades, which scratch the glass. Rinse well, then dry and polish each pane with a lint-free cloth until it's streak-free. Clean the inside of the door frame too, and check the vents for grease. Take your time with the corners. A thin, damp cloth wrapped around a ruler can help you reach narrow spots.
steps.tip: Baking soda paste for burnt spots
steps.imagePrompt: A hand wiping a clean glass pane with a microfiber cloth over a kitchen towel, bright light, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Reassemble in the same order
steps.narration: Step six. Put the panes back in the reverse order that you took them out, using your photos. Make sure that each pane sits in its slot or clip, with the same orientation, and that any rubber spacers or gaskets are in place. Then put on the top trim, and tighten the screws gently, just until snug. Over-tightening can crack the glass. Run your finger along the edge to make sure everything is level, and wipe away fingerprints. Take a final look through the glass in the light, since dust or smears are easy to see before the door is closed up.
steps.imagePrompt: Hands fitting the top trim back onto a reassembled oven door lying on a towel, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Refit the door and test
steps.narration: Step seven. Hold the door at the same shallow angle as before, and slide the hinge arms back into the slots on the oven. Push the door fully down, then open it all the way and flip the hinge locks back to their normal positions. Close and open the door a few times to check that it moves smoothly and shuts tightly. Switch the power back on, and run the oven for a few minutes. Check that the door seals properly. Take care to hold the door with both hands. Once it is back, the oven should look like new.
steps.mistake: Closing the door with the hinge locks on
steps.imagePrompt: A clean oven door being refitted onto the hinges, bright kitchen, photorealistic, no text

bonus.label: STILL STUCK?
bonus.title: If the glass stays cloudy
bonus.narration: If the glass is still cloudy after washing, check each pane on both sides. Many doors have three layers, and the film can sit on a surface you skipped. A haze that survives a careful wash is usually etching, damage from years of grease and strong cleaners, and it cannot be polished away. In that case, order replacement glass from the maker using your oven's model number.
bonus.imagePrompt: A hand holding a clean glass oven door pane up to a window to check for haze, a folded towel and a small screw cup on the kitchen table in the background. 16:9 landscape format. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark.

bonus.label: CALL A PRO
bonus.title: When to call a technician
bonus.narration: Some situations call for a technician. Hinge springs are under tension, so if the door will not release or snaps back when you remove it, stop and call. If you have a gas oven and smell gas at any point, leave the house, and call your gas emergency number from outside. Do not switch anything on or off, and stay out until it is safe.
bonus.imagePrompt: A technician in work gloves crouching in front of a freestanding oven with its door open, a screwdriver in one hand and a small toolbox on the floor, no face visible. 16:9 landscape format. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark.

bonus.label: KEEP IT CLEAN
bonus.title: Keep grease off the glass
bonus.narration: A few habits keep grease from building up again. Cover roasting dishes with a lid or loose foil, so fat does not spit onto the glass. Put a baking sheet on the lower rack to catch drips. Wipe the inside of the door after it has cooled, while spills are still soft. Do not rub the rubber seal around the door, because cleaners can damage it.
bonus.imagePrompt: A clean oven with its door open showing a lower rack with a baking sheet, a covered roasting dish on the middle rack, bright kitchen light. 16:9 landscape format. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark.

mistakesToAvoid.narration: Here are the mistakes to avoid. First, rushing without reading your manual or taking photos. If you can't remember how the parts fit, reassembly is hard. Second, using abrasive tools or razor blades on the glass, which leave scratches that trap grease. And third, forcing parts that don't want to move. If something sticks, stop and check the instructions, or ask a technician. Safety comes first with ovens, glass and hinges. If anything feels unsafe, a technician can do this job quickly.

recap.narration: Let's recap. Switch off the oven and let it cool. Remove the door, using the hinge locks. Open the top trim. Slide out the glass panes. Wash and dry each pane. Reassemble in the same order. And refit the door and test it. Seven steps, about forty minutes, and an oven door you can see through again. If the glass stays cloudy, replace it, and call a technician if anything feels unsafe.

Open the top of the door

outro: That's how you clean between the glass on your oven door. If your oven window is clear again, subscribe to WikiTube, because we publish a new how-to every single day. Tell us in the comments how greasy your oven was, and what you would like us to explain next. See you tomorrow.

metadata.title: How to Clean Between the Glass on Your Oven Door
metadata.description:
Grease stuck between the glass panes of your oven door? In this step-by-step video you'll learn how to clean between the glass on your oven door safely: cool the oven, take photos, remove the door using the hinge locks, open the top trim, slide out the glass panes, wash and dry them, reassemble in the right order and refit the door. Check your manual first, since models differ slightly.

You'll need: a screwdriver, dish soap and warm water, microfiber cloths, a large towel, your oven manual.

short.title: Clean between your oven door glass #shorts

short.hook: Grease trapped inside your oven door? Here is how to reach it.

steps.title: Lock and lift
steps.narration: One. With the oven cool, lock the hinges and lift the door off. Take photos.

steps.title: Open the trim
steps.narration: Two. Remove the top screws, lift the trim, and slide out the glass panes.

steps.title: Wash and rebuild
steps.narration: Three. Wash each pane with soapy water, then reassemble in the same order.
